title: Require agreement of complete syndrome vectors in the actual noisy schedule
statement: A complete 3x3 Bacon-Shor round measures six horizontal XX gauges and six vertical ZZ gauges, using 18 physical H gates and known phase corrections. Three-gauge products give the FULL four-bit stabilizer syndrome. Repeat until TWO consecutive COMPLETE vectors agree, with a four-round cap; otherwise flag without a speculative correction. Apply the ordinary row/column Pauli frame on acceptance. Clean encoded input with at most ONE localized bad location leaves at most a correctable error modulo gauge and accepts within four rounds. One correctable input error with NO new fault is corrected after two rounds; the theorem does not admit both. The faulty round may report any of 16 vectors. Adjacent equality includes a fault-free round and avoids the retained bitwise-majority failure 00,01,11. Coherent errors use the actual subsystem span and ideal good rounds. The source checked 6,400 scheduled histories, 3,200 encountered before stopping, with no admitted violations or flags. This is a bounded recovery construction, not a threshold. Encoded input, controller reliability, localization and actual reset/isolation are explicit.
